text:
cora: customer reports intermittent TLS handshake failures (502/502 with TLS alert unrecognized_name) when talking to Redwood hosted API from their VPC via a VPCE. ~5-7% of requests fail, mostly from a subset of pods. They have corporate outbound proxy + strict NACLs. Repro steps they gave:

cora: repro gist:
```
# pod exec
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/complete -H 'Host: api.redwood.example' --resolve api.redwood.example:443:192.0.2.45
* Connected to 192.0.2.45 (192.0.2.45) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using ...
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS alert, fatal unrecognized_name
* closing connection 0
curl: (35) error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert unexpected message
```

cora: notes: the IP above is the vpce interface IP. Some client pods resolve to that IP, others to a public IP (via their corporate DNS forwarder). Failures line up with the ones resolving to the vpce IP but then getting proxied. attaching route table, sg, nacl dumps below.

ashwin: can you paste the route table + resolver rules and a dig from one failing pod and a succeeding pod? also want tcpdump from the pod if possible. suspect split-horizon / DNS caching + egress policy ordering. :thinking:

cora: route table excerpt:
```
RTB-0abcd: subnet-10.10.1.0/24 -> local
route: 192.0.2.45/32 -> eni/vpce-0abcde (explicit host route)
route: 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-012345 (default)
```

cora: NACL outbound rules (stateless):
```
100: ALLOW tcp 0.0.0.0/0 80
110: ALLOW tcp 0.0.0.0/0 443
120: DENY tcp 0.0.0.0/0 32768-65535   # ephemeral range blocked by policy
```

cora: dig from failing pod:
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.example
192.0.2.45
```

cora: dig from working pod:
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.example
198.51.100.12
```

cora: tcpdump from failing pod during a failed handshake shows SYN -> 192.0.2.45:443 (src port 49152) then nothing back. packet capture on host shows SYN/ACK from 192.0.2.45 but it never reaches pod.

ashwin: that NACL DENY on ephemeral ports is the smoking gun. NACLs are stateless: when the server sends a reply to src port 49152, the NACL must allow inbound ephemeral port range. If outbound rule denies that range, replies are dropped. This explains why the pod initiates the handshake but sees no response (or sees proxy responses mismatched). Also the mixed DNS results indicate some pods resolved to public IP (go through NAT/proxy) and others to VPCE IP (direct). The ones that go direct need ephemeral ports allowed both ways.

jie: adding to that — some proxies rewrite SNI when traffic hits NAT/proxy and cause unrecognized_name. If a pod is routed via the corporate proxy (public IP path) it will often succeed because the proxy rewrites headers; the direct path to the VPCE expects the original SNI. Mixed resolution + stateless NACL denies cause flaky TLS failures.

cora: proposed remediation we gave customer:
- remove/allow ephemeral range in NACL (32768-65535) for both inbound/outbound on the subnet
- or add an explicit NACL rule to allow ephemeral ports to/from the VPCE IP only (more conservative)
- short-term workaround: purge DNS caches on kube-dns / pods so all resolve to the same view, or add a stub-resolver rule that pins api.redwood.example -> 192.0.2.45 consistently
- optionally add a more specific route precedence: host route to vpce is already present but ensure no flapping by checking DHCP option set / resolver rules

ashwin: also asked customer to confirm whether any intermediary (proxy/firewall) does TLS termination for the public IP path; we suggested adding VPCE IP to their proxy bypass list so direct traffic to VPCE isn't intercepted.

anna: ran a quick verification script for them and recommended exact tcpdump filter + commands to validate after change:
```
sudo tcpdump -i any host 192.0.2.45 and port 443 -w /tmp/vpce-handshake.pcap
# on pod
curl -v --resolve api.redwood.example:443:192.0.2.45 https://api.redwood.example/v1/complete
```

cora: customer applied ephemeral allow rule for the subnet and flushed kube-dns cache (kubectl delete pod -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-dns). they also added VPCE IP to proxy bypass.

cora: update: 48h post-change, they report no TLS unrecognized_name errors, error rate back to baseline. customer accepted the NACL-change plan and will keep the proxy bypass for the VPCE CIDR. :thumbsup:

ashwin: leaving note for eng-runtime: consider adding a KB entry for "mixed DNS + stateless NACL ephemeral port denial causing TLS handshake failures with VPCE" and include the tcpdump + dig repro steps. tagging @jie for a short doc + checklist to share with customers who use corporate proxies.

jie: ack — will draft KB and add a recommended ephemeral port snippet and DNS cache purge steps.

sre-bot: incident-note: ticket #123456 closed after customer's confirmation. root cause: outbound NACL blocked ephemeral ports combined with inconsistent DNS resolution leading to mixed proxy/direct flows and TLS SNI mismatches.

cora: closing thread — will follow up with KB link once available.
